key_insight: A trainable quantum circuit can be used as a binary classifier for images and low-dimensional features, with performance depending strongly on circuit depth, optimizer choice, and dataset size.
engineering_relevance: This work gives a practical blueprint for implementing and benchmarking quantum machine-learning classifiers against classical baselines on real binary tasks.
method: Encode MNIST zeros vs ones and collider event data into a parameterized quantum circuit (Ansatz).
Train the circuit with multiple minimizers and vary the number of layers to study optimization behavior.
Evaluate using ROC curves, AUC, confusion matrices, and test accuracy; compare image results with a small CNN.
evidence_signal: The paper tests on two binary datasets—MNIST and collider events with/without pile-up—using train/test splits and reports ROC, AUC, confusion matrices, and test accuracy.
watch_item: Results are sensitive to circuit depth, optimizer, and data representation, so scaling to larger problems may face performance and hardware-simulation limits.
paper_title: Towards the implementation of a quantum classifier
